page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.large is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, built on KVM virtualization. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. It includes 8.0 GB of memory, delivering a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network block volumes for persistent disk storage, while network throughput is provisioned at a baseline rate of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent single-threaded execution paired with restrained multi-core and memory throughput. Single-core performance falls within average ranges, recording 1,519.0 points in Geekbench single-core, 1,880.59 in stress-ng single-core, and 27.64 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics place in the lowest ten percent of comparable servers, yielding 1,931.67 in stress-ng multi-core and 1,774.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 14.51 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 13.41 GB/sec for writes, resulting in a weak PassMark memory score of 1,629.41.

Given its dual-vCPU capacity and lack of local NVMe storage, the ecs.g7nex.large offers a cost-conscious entry point for dedicated-core infrastructure, avoiding multi-tenant CPU throttling. It is best suited for entry-level enterprise web serving, lightweight backend services, microservices, and modest Redis caching tiers, but it is not intended for database workloads requiring intensive I/O operations or highly parallel data processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7nex.large is a general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz under KVM virtualization. Based on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 extensions, it maintains a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal average single-core computing capabilities, including a 1,519.0 Geekbench single-core score and steady compression rates, alongside lower-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth figures due to its single physical core constraint. With no bundled storage, persistent data relies entirely on attached cloud disks. The server represents an economical dedicated-core configuration suitable for lightweight web serving, application middleware, background worker processes, and small-scale caching layers.
